topic: Factorisation of Quadratic Expressions of the Form x² + bx + c and ax² + bx + c

lessonData.topic: Factorisation of Quadratic Expressions of the Form x² + bx + c and ax² + bx + c
lessonData.subject: Mathematics / Geometry
lessonData.tagline: Unlock the algebra code: turn trinomial puzzles into smooth binomial products!
lessonData.overview: Factorising a quadratic trinomial reverses expansion by breaking an algebraic expression into two linear binomial factors. By identifying integer factor pairs that multiply to the constant product and sum to the middle coefficient, students learn to systematically factorise both monic and non-monic quadratics.

diagram.title: Quadratic Factorisation Decision Workflow
diagram.description: Step-by-step pathway to factorise any quadratic expression completely and accurately.

nodes.label: Extract Common Factor
nodes.details: Always extract any common numerical or variable factor first, especially a negative sign if the x² term is negative.

nodes.label: Identify Leading Coefficient
nodes.details: Determine whether the expression is monic (a = 1) or non-monic (a ≠ 1) to pick the most efficient strategy.

nodes.label: Product-Sum Rule
nodes.details: Find two integers whose product equals the constant c and whose sum equals the middle coefficient b.

nodes.label: AC Split Method
nodes.details: Find two numbers whose product is a × c and sum is b, then split the middle term into two distinct terms.

nodes.label: Multiplication Frame / Grouping
nodes.details: Group the four terms into two pairs or arrange them in a 2x2 grid to factor out common binomials.

nodes.label: Factored Binomial Product
nodes.details: Write out the final factored form and verify by expanding via FOIL.

chalkNotes.title: Factorisation of Quadratics
chalkNotes.subtitle: x² + bx + c and ax² + bx + c
chalkNotes.coreRuleOrFormula: ax² + bx + c = a(x - p)(x - q)  |  Find numbers with Product = a × c and Sum = b
bulletPoints: Rule 1 (Monic): For x² + bx + c, find two numbers p and q such that p × q = c and p + q = b.
Sign Clues: If c > 0 and b > 0 → (+)(+); if c > 0 and b < 0 → (-)(-); if c < 0 → (+)(-).
Rule 2 (Non-monic): For ax² + bx + c, find two factors of a × c that add to b, then split the middle term bx.
Two-variable trinomials: Treat x² + 5xy - 6y² like x² + 5x - 6 = (x - 1)(x + 6), then attach y to get (x - y)(x + 6y).
keyTakeaways: Crucial Step 0: Always extract common factors (especially -1 if the leading term is negative) before starting.
Constant term is the PRODUCT; middle coefficient is the SUM—never swap them!

quiz.question: A student attempts to factorise 2x² + 7x - 15. They find that the product of the diagonal terms is 2 × (-15) = -30. Which two terms should replace +7x, and what is the resulting factored expression?
quiz.explanation: We need two numbers that multiply to -30 and add to +7. The factors are +10 and -3, because 10 × (-3) = -30 and 10 + (-3) = +7. Splitting 7x into 10x - 3x gives: 2x² + 10x - 3x - 15 = 2x(x + 5) - 3(x + 5) = (2x - 3)(x + 5).

suggestedQuestions: What is the highest common factor (HCF) of the terms 8x²y and 12xy² before we factorise?
List all integer factor pairs of -24 that add up to +5.
How do we handle factorising an expression like -x² + 6x - 9 where the coefficient of x² is negative?

factorisation-of-quadratic-expressions-o.title: Factoring Quadratic Expressions

nodes.label: Quadratic Trinomial
nodes.details: Identify the leading coefficient 'a', middle coefficient 'b', and constant 'c'.

nodes.label: Simple Trinomial (a = 1)
nodes.sublabel: Find numbers: p + q = b, p × q = c
nodes.details: Look for two integers that multiply to give 'c' and add up to give 'b'.

nodes.label: General Trinomial (a ≠ 1)
nodes.details: Find two numbers multiplying to 'ac' and adding to 'b', then split the middle term and factor by grouping.

nodes.label: Product of Binomials
nodes.details: The expression is written in fully factorised form as two linear factors.

key-properties-of-factorisation-of-quadr.title: Properties of Factoring Quadratic Expressions
key-properties-of-factorisation-of-quadr.description: A guide showing the core rules and methods for factoring both monic (x² + bx + c) and non-monic (ax² + bx + c) quadratics.

nodes.label: Quadratic Expression
nodes.details: A second-degree polynomial that factors into two linear binomials (px + m)(qx + n).

nodes.label: Simple Monic: x² + bx + c
nodes.details: Find two integers p and q that multiply to c and add to b to write factors directly as (x + p)(x + q).

nodes.label: General Form: ax² + bx + c
nodes.sublabel: Split Middle Term using a × c
nodes.details: Find two integers that multiply to a × c and sum to b, split the middle term, and factor by grouping.

nodes.label: Sign Determinant Rules
nodes.details: If the constant product is positive, both signs match b; if negative, the binomials have opposite signs.

main.title: Factorisation by Multiplication Frame
main.why: It allows the learner to visualize how an area model physically maps the components of a quadratic expression back into its factors.
main.checkQuestion: If we look at the multiplication frame, why do the horizontal and vertical labels multiply to fill the boxes inside?

steps.name: Find row common factors

steps.name: Find column common factors
steps.caption: Now find the highest common factor for each column to complete the factors.

steps.name: Write the solution
steps.caption: The sides of the frame give us our final factors: (2x - 3) and (x + 5).
